ui.mod_editor_help_metadata_body:
What G3M saves

G3M stores a mod in mod_config.json. The Mod ID identifies it locally and in dependencies or conflicts. It must stay stable after publishing. Name, version, authors, description, homepage, icon, tags, and game version describe the mod in the library and mod browser.

One author per line.
ui.mod_editor_help_placeholders_body:
Built-in placeholders

Start a portable path with one built-in placeholder, then a slash and the path below it. Built-in names are reserved.

  • ${mod_path}: this mod's folder. Use it for sources, icons, and custom placeholder paths. It cannot be a target root.
  • ${game_path}: the selected game's installation folder.
  • ${game_data_path}: the selected game's data folder.
  • ${user_path}: the current operating system user's home folder.

Examples: ${mod_path}/assets/logo.png and ${game_path}/data.win.

Archive paths

Supported archives can be sources. Writable formats can also be targets. Add a slash after the archive filename to address its contents. ${mod_path}/assets.zip/ means the archive root. ${mod_path}/assets.zip/images/icon.png means one file inside that archive.
ui.mod_editor_help_custom_placeholders_body:
Reusable path roots

Create a custom placeholder once, then use it at the beginning of a source or target path as ${name}/…. Names use English letters, numbers, and underscores. They start with a letter and must be unique.

Its path starts with exactly one built-in root and a path suffix. For example, assets = ${mod_path}/assets. A custom placeholder cannot contain another custom placeholder. A target cannot use a custom placeholder that points inside ${mod_path}.

Changing a custom placeholder changes every operation that uses it. Replace all uses before removing it.
ui.mod_editor_help_operations_body:
Operation types

  • Info records a documentation file and does not change the game.
  • Patch applies a patch file to an existing target file.
  • Overwrite copies a file or folder and replaces conflicting files.
  • Soft-Overwrite copies only where no target file already exists.
  • Hard-Overwrite removes its destination before copying. With a file target, it clears the target file's parent folder before copying.
  • Extract copies the contents of a source folder or archive into a target folder.
  • Soft-Extract extracts only missing files.
  • Hard-Extract clears the target folder before extracting.

G3M validates each source and target, then executes the ordered operations. Use Soft variants to preserve existing files. Use Hard variants only when the mod must fully control the destination.
ui.mod_editor_help_order_body:
Execution order

G3M processes operations from top to bottom. A group's contents are processed in their displayed order before the next item outside that group.
ui.mod_editor_help_compatibility_body:
Compatibility

Dependencies list mods that must be installed. Conflicts list mods that cannot be used together. Leave Order as No order unless a relative load position is required. Before and After choose the mod order. The step and priority options choose the required stage or position within that stage.

Hashes

Source and target hashes store a SHA-256 fingerprint. When enabled, G3M verifies the file before applying the operation and stops if it no longer matches. Use them when a patch or replacement depends on an exact game or source version.
